title: The YM2612 registers
covers: the registers of the YM2612 (OPN2) in both banks, as Yamaha's data sheet for its CMOS version, the YM3438, lists them, and what MAME does for each

rows.text: The description lists $21, together with $2C, as test information; the glyphs of the word after the first one are garbled in the capture.
The description says to keep it always in the state 0; the glyphs around the 0 are garbled in the capture.
The register map comments $21 as LSI Test Data.
The description says $22 controls LFO ON/OFF.
The description says $22 sets the LFO oscillation frequency; the glyphs of the frequency word are garbled in the capture.
The register map comments $22 as LFO FREQ CONTROL.
The capture lists the map's addresses and its comments as two columns in the same order; the second of each is $22 and LFO FREQ CONTROL.
The description gives $24 to $26 as one range and names timer A and timer B; the glyphs of the words saying what they set are garbled in the capture.
The register map comments $24 as Timer-A's 8 bits.
The register map comments $25 as Timer-A's lower 2 bits.
The register map comments $26 as Timer-B's data.
The description names $27 and says it controls the operation of timers A and B and sets the mode of FM channel 3; several glyphs are garbled in the capture.
The register map comments $27 as the Timer-A/B Control and the 3CH Mode.
MAME does not store a write of 0x27 at once: it hands the byte to a scheduler synchronisation, and the store happens when the engine's mode-write handler runs.
Register $28 is the key on/off register.
A write to register $28 is for key on/off.
The description says DATA is written directly to the DAC; the capture lists $2A far from this line, so the pairing follows the order of the page's table.
The register map comments $2A as DAC Data.
The capture lists the map's addresses and its comments as two columns in the same order; the eighth of each is $2A and DAC Data.
MAME takes a write to 0x2A as the byte with its bit 7 inverted, shifted left once, and stores it in bits 8 to 1 of its DAC data.
The description says $2B selects whether channel 6 outputs its FM sound or the DATA written to $2A; the glyphs of the output word are garbled.
The register map comments $2B as DAC Select.
The capture lists the map's addresses and its comments as two columns in the same order; the ninth of each is $2B and DAC Select.
MAME stores bit 7 of the byte written to 0x2B as its DAC enable.
MAME adds the DAC value to output 0 when bit 7 of register 0x1B6 is set and to output 1 when bit 6 is set.
MAME's YM2612 output passes the DAC value through a discontinuity offset, 3 below zero and 4 otherwise; its YM3438 output takes the sign-extended DAC data as it is.
The register map comments $2C as LSI Test Data.
The capture lists the map's addresses and its comments as two columns in the same order; the tenth of each is $2C and LSI Test Data.
MAME does not pass a write to 0x2C to the FM registers: it copies bit 3 of the byte into the lowest bit of its DAC data.
The description says $30 to $3E hold the control of Detune and Multiple.
It adds that this is used when setting a timbre and controls the relation of the fundamental to its overtones; several glyphs are garbled in the capture.
The description says $40 to $4E give Total Level.
It adds that this information becomes the volume of the modulated wave and the modulation index of the modulating wave; several glyphs are garbled.
The description says $50 to $5E hold Key-Scale and Attack Rate.
Key-Scale controls how A, D, S and R change with pitch information; Attack Rate gives the envelope's rate of change at attack; some glyphs are garbled.
The description says $60 to $6E hold Decay Rate and the amplitude modulation ON/OFF; the glyphs of amplitude are garbled in the capture.
Decay Rate is the rate at which the envelope changes at decay; a few glyphs of the line are garbled.
The description says $70 to $7E hold Sustain Rate.
Sustain Rate is the rate at which the envelope changes at sustain; one glyph of the line is garbled.
The register map gives $80 to $8E to Sustain Level and Release Rate, and $83, $87 and $8B have no address.
Sustain Level gives the level at which the envelope moves from decay to sustain.
Release Rate gives the rate at which the envelope changes at release.
MAME expands a cached sustain level of 15 to 31, so the four-bit field acts as five bits.
The register map gives $90 to $9E to SSG-type envelope control, with $93, $97 and $9B absent.
It gives the envelope a preset shape; several glyphs of the line are garbled in the capture.
MAME reads D3 as the SSG-EG enable and, when it is set, inverts the envelope at key on if mode bit D2 is set.
The register map gives $A0 to $A6 to each channel's key code, the F-Number.
The map names the two fields F-Num 1 and BLOCK F-Num 2.
MAME stores nothing for a write to $A3 or $A7: the handler returns before any store.
MAME latches a write to $A4 to $A6 and applies it only when the lower byte at $A0 to $A2 is written.
The register map gives $A8 to $AE to the F-Numbers of the special mode, whose key codes the description gives.
The map names the mode 3CH-3Slot and its fields 3CH F-Num 1 and 3CH BLOCK F-Num 2.
MAME replaces the frequency of three of the third channel's four operators with $A9/$AD, $AA/$AE and $A8/$AC when register 0x27 selects multi-frequency mode.
MAME stores nothing for a write to $AB or $AF: the handler returns before any store.
MAME latches a write to $AC to $AE and applies it only when the lower byte at $A8 to $AA is written.
The register map gives $B0 to $B2 to the self-feedback and the connection.
The description says they give the FM modulation form (Connection) and the depth of the feedback FM (Self-feedback).
MAME reads the feedback from bits 3 to 5 and the algorithm from bits 0 to 2 of the byte.
MAME picks one of eight operator connections from the algorithm bits, by table lookup.
The register map gives $B4 to $B6 to the L/R output selection and the LFO depth on amplitude and frequency.
The map names the three fields LR, AMS and PMS.
MAME reads the left output bit at D7 and the right at D6, and adds a channel to a side only when its bit is set.
MAME shifts the LFO value by 7, 3, 1 or 0 for AMS, and PM depth 0 leaves the phase unmodulated.
MAME reads register 0x30 plus the operator offset, which adds 0x100 for the second group of 12 operators.
MAME stores the byte written to this range in the FM register array at that register number.
MAME takes a write to the upper address port as 0x100 ORed with the data, and its upper data port hands the register to the FM engine.

searched.gave: ymfm_opn.h and ymopn.h cite no manual; the comments list the register bit layout and say it applies at address+100 on OPNA+.
Yamaha's own YM3438 data sheet, already in the table, is the maker's document; its port table names channels 4 to 6.
Its Yamaha folder lists YM2149, YM2151, YM2203, YM2413, YM3439 and YM3613 sheets; it has no YM2612 or YM3438 sheet.
The archive.org item yamaha-chip-jpn is the table's archive copy of the YM3438 data sheet.
No datasheet index was consulted: the maker's data sheet for the chip is already in the table.
